name: Everest Group, Ltd.
moat_justification: Global reinsurance treaty franchise (CR 87-88% in H1 2026) and a growing wholesale/specialty book are real, but (re)insurance capacity is close to a commodity: no network effects, low switching costs, price set by the cycle. Returns confirm it - net income on year-end equity was ~19% in the clean year 2023 but only ~10% in 2024 and 2025 after casualty reserve charges (~$1.7B in 2024, $478M more in Q3 2025), i.e. returns through the recent cycle sit near the cost of capital, not well above it. roic_proxy and gross margin are not computable for this filer (no operating-income/COGS tags for an insurer); ROE on filing net income and equity is the substitute evidence.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

DEBT_TAGS_BLANK: no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year — net debt is UNKNOWN (not zero); no leverage verdict is possible from the engine, state the balance sheet from the filing in analysis.md
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-26), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows: the investing-activities section lists only fixed-maturity/equity/other-invested-asset flows, the net change in short-term investments and unsettled securities transactions, and proceeds from sale of renewal rights - there is no purchases-of-property-and-equipment (or any capex) line for FY2025, FY2024 or FY2023, and the balance sheet carries no property-and-equipment line. The statement fully reconciles without one: FY2025 operating $3,068M + investing $(2,096)M + financing $(1,175)M + FX $(28)M = the reported net decrease in cash of $(231)M exactly; FY2024: $4,957M - $4,478M - $383M + $16M = reported $112M exactly; FY2023: $4,553M - $5,902M + $1,409M - $23M = $37M vs reported $38M (rounding). EDGAR companyfacts for CIK 1095073 contains no capex fact under any candidate tag in any year.); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.2x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier C (12.9%) vs bull-case tier A (20.7%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Global reinsurer mid-cleanup: quality treaty core (91.7% FY2025 CR, 87-88% in H1 2026) but the OCF base capitalizes float and the exited U.S. casualty book still sits on $34.3B of reserves after ~$2.2B of 2024-25 charges - B by numbers (16.7% weighted IRR, IV@15% $444 vs $389 price), sized down to C per the insurer-float rule and the bear end (C) of the tier band; clears 15% only below ~$444 on these inputs.
exit_alert_suppressed_reason: sector model misfit; tier exists only because of a judgment override
tier_override_reason: Insurer-float softening (Andrew's standing rule, 2026-10-15; same treatment as PFG/HIG/ACGL/WRB): the OCF-based OE base capitalizes float - the engine-native median base ($109.06/share) capitalizes the 2023-24 premium-growth years outright (zero-fill weighted IRR 33.3%, a fake Tier S), and even the TTM base used ($48.98/share) is OCF on a book whose loss reserves grew to $34,312M while the exited casualty book is still paying out. NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE is structural in 2023, 2024 and 2025. Tier by numbers B (16.7% weighted) therefore overstates distributable owner's earnings; softened one notch to C, which is also the bear end of the TIER_BAND (bear C 12.9% / bull A 20.7%). Confidence low (SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH + WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD 4.2x).
moat_for: Top-tier global reinsurance treaty franchise - 87.2%/88.5% combined ratio in Q1/Q2 2026, 91.7% for FY2025
Scale: $45.4B investments and cash, $15.5B equity, S&P 500 member, A+ range financial strength ratings
Mt. Logan Re sidecar gives fee income and third-party capital leverage on cat business
Wholesale & specialty pivot is working - specialty premiums +32.9% in Q1 2026, mid-80s attritional CR
moat_against: Reserve credibility damaged: ~$1.7B casualty reserve charge in 2024 and $478M more in Q3 2025; $34.3B loss reserves still carry the exited retail book's tail
Reinsurance pricing is cyclical and capacity-driven - no durable pricing power; property cat pricing softening in 2026 renewals
Social inflation on U.S. casualty is an industry-wide, unmodelable drag that Everest under-reserved for years
Returns through the cycle (~10% ROE 2024-25) sit near the cost of capital, not above it
